question: Why did the official uncertainty on Newton's constant G grow about twelvefold in 1998?
answer: Because one careful laboratory disagreed. In 1995 PTB, Germany's national standards institute, reported a G about 0.6% above the accepted value, far outside everyone's error bars. With no fault found in it, CODATA, which sets the recommended constants, widened its uncertainty from about 0.013% to 0.15%. Later measurements did not repeat the German value.
move: An honest error bar can grow even as the evidence improves.

diagram.caption: One result sat 0.6% off, forty-six times the old error bars; the bars widened twelvefold.

source: Mohr & Taylor, Reviews of Modern Physics, 2000
reference: Mohr & Taylor, CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 1998, Reviews of Modern Physics 72, 351, 2000
